scope: Dated public research fixtures for preparing, but not executing, a 14-day paid-demand validation experiment for quota-to-cash. Agency service descriptions and public demand signals are hypotheses, not qualified buyers, outreach permission, payment commitments or revenue. Personal handles are replaced with neutral labels; public source URLs remain for verification. No live outreach, purchases, monetization changes or scheduled execution are represented.

sources.title: Apify Store Publishing Terms and Conditions
sources.evidence_summary: Public Actors are available in Store. The terms restrict off-platform product or service promotion in Store content and non-Apify payment gateways. Verified Creator status requires KYC. Reported profit can change after refunds or unpaid invoices.
sources.limitations: Last-updated date, not original publication date. This is an operational summary, not legal advice. Section 10.3.2 mentions a USD 20 PayPal minimum and USD 100 for other methods; the payout documentation separately includes Wise in its USD 20 group. Confirm the applicable method in Console.

sources.title: Monetize Actors
sources.evidence_summary: PPE supports programmatically triggered paid events. Analytics distinguish paid and free users. Per-request agentic payments require PPE without additional platform-usage billing, limited permissions, no Standby mode, and completed creator KYC.
sources.limitations: Availability of these features for this project's current account has not been checked. Agentic-payment eligibility is not evidence of discovery, customer demand, or revenue.

sources.title: Set up Actor monetization
sources.evidence_summary: Billing and payment details precede monetization setup. Significant pricing changes normally require 14 days and are limited to one per month; the documentation says the waiting period does not apply if the Actor has no paying users.
sources.limitations: No billing, payout, or monetization configuration was read or changed. The experiment should freeze its initial price rather than assume unrestricted daily price increases.

sources.title: Actor pricing and costs
sources.evidence_summary: The documented profit formula is 0.8 times event revenue minus platform costs. Only paid-plan users' revenue and costs count; free-plan usage produces no creator revenue and its platform cost is covered by Apify.
sources.limitations: A paid-plan flag is a revenue-eligibility signal, not proof that a particular customer's invoice has settled. The experiment's actual compute, storage, and transfer costs remain unmeasured.

sources.title: Manage payouts
sources.evidence_summary: Payout eligibility requires billing details, a payment method, and identity verification. Previous-month invoices issue on day 11, are automatically approved on day 14 if untouched, and payouts issue on days 21-25. Thresholds are USD 20 for PayPal/Wise and USD 100 otherwise.
sources.limitations: The Store terms do not separately list Wise under the USD 20 threshold. Payouts depend on legitimate already-paid users, thresholds, KYC, reviews, and transfer processing. A 14-day demand experiment cannot promise cash receipt.

sources.title: Pay-per-event pricing model
sources.evidence_summary: The platform provides automatically charged start and default-dataset-item events. Results should be saved and accessible before billing. Users set maximum run costs; charging and processing must respect those limits.
sources.limitations: The proposed USD 0.01 start plus USD 0.002 per delivered record is this project's experiment hypothesis, not Apify's prescribed price. Verify synthetic versus custom charging to avoid duplicate charges.

sources.title: GitHub Acceptable Use Policies
sources.evidence_summary: Project-related promotional links or text may appear in the owner's README or project description. Advertising in other users' accounts, excessive automated bulk activity, and using collected user information for unsolicited email or spam are prohibited.
sources.limitations: Permission for project-related README content is not permission for automated prospecting, mass issue creation, fake stars, or unsolicited messages. Relevant project content must remain the repository's main purpose.

sources.title: Apify MCP server
sources.evidence_summary: External agents can discover and run Store Actors through MCP. Apify AI shares the search/execution backend. Ranking uses factors similar to Actor quality score; full-permission Actors are excluded.
sources.limitations: Search inclusion, position, third-party agent adoption, and payment for this Actor have not been verified. Discovery checks can use public search/detail tools; paid runs require separate authorization and must never count as customer demand when self-funded.

sources.title: Actor-to-Actor integrations
sources.evidence_summary: Integration-ready Actors can receive another Actor's output. Store has an Integrations category for these targets, and users can add a target from an Actor's Integrations tab.
sources.limitations: This project's integration-ready configuration and catalog eligibility have not been audited. Compatibility documentation does not grant permission to advertise on another creator's issues or alter another user's workflow.

sources.title: Find the right Apify Expert
sources.evidence_summary: The official directory lists certified scraping and automation providers with public service descriptions. Some explicitly offer data cleaning, normalization, schema alignment, CRM cleanup, or Apify/Make integration.
sources.limitations: Directory membership, accepting clients, and public contact details do not establish buying intent or consent to automated sales outreach. Do not invent procurement budgets or claim partnership.

sources.title: Becoming an n8n template creator and getting help
sources.evidence_summary: Templates are submitted through creator accounts under Creator Hub guidelines. New creators submit one template at a time. Review usually takes up to a week; three approved templates qualify for verified status.
sources.limitations: The complete Creator Hub submission rules and permission for unattended AI submissions were not verified. Do not extrapolate template submission permission from this help page or confuse it with forum posting permission.

sources.title: Apify Community Code of Conduct
sources.evidence_summary: Links must be relevant and explained, not posted simply to attract traffic. Unsolicited links to one's own project in other users' threads, cross-posting, and content-free bumps are discouraged or prohibited by the community standards.
sources.limitations: The effective date is explicit. Server-specific permissions for AI bots or promotional channels have not been verified; missing prohibition is not affirmative permission.

sources.title: Automated User Accounts (Self-Bots)
sources.evidence_summary: Discord offers separate bot accounts. Automating normal user accounts outside the OAuth2/bot API is forbidden and can result in account termination.
sources.limitations: A compliant bot account still needs a server's permission and must follow its rules. This does not authorize cold DMs, spam, or installing bots in servers controlled by others.

sources.title: This forum is for humans, by humans
sources.evidence_summary: The official announcement prohibits AI-produced forum questions and replies posted without the poster's own understanding and engagement. AI-generated material can be removed as spam.
sources.limitations: This rules out the proposed no-human forum posting workflow. It does not prohibit private AI research or establish the separate template library's rules.

sources.title: Make Community: Do's and Don'ts
sources.evidence_summary: Current rules prohibit AI-generated responses and automated content of any kind. Promotion is restricted to Hire a Pro, with one Offer Help service topic per person; selling or solicitation in other posts or DMs is prohibited.
sources.limitations: The displayed date is the original topic date; later policy edits are not separately dated in the retrieved view. These are current retrieved rules, not a claim that the AI provision existed in 2021.

sources.title: Hacker News Guidelines
sources.evidence_summary: Guidelines prohibit generated or AI-edited text and automated posting. Users should not use HN primarily for promotion or solicit votes, comments, or submissions.
sources.limitations: This is a clear exclusion from unattended AI distribution, even though generic Actor-marketing checklists recommend HN. Public reading can still inform research.

leads.name: Enhance Tech Solutions
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its Apify profile offers e-commerce scraping, product and price tracking, analytics feeds, schema alignment for GTINs, product IDs and retailer feeds, and data cleaning with version-controlled mappings.
leads.fit_inference: A possible technical interview or delivery partnership candidate for repeatable post-scrape cleanup and acceptance checks. Its existing services overlap substantially with the proposed offer; willingness to buy is unverified.
leads.product_gap: The published catalog example uses a fixed schema. The workbench supports validated flat-field ToolSpec mappings, but does not supply general GTIN or retailer-feed semantics, taxonomy management, or a production feed integration.
leads.qualification_question: Do you have a recurring product JSON cleanup step whose input, expected output and acceptance rules could be demonstrated with a redacted sample?

leads.name: Makeitfuture
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its product enrichment service covers supplier feeds, structured product attributes, missing fields, duplicate catalogue content, Merchant Center feed fields, and connections to stores, PIM and ERP systems.
leads.fit_inference: A possible workflow feedback, referral or tool procurement candidate for deterministic cleanup and acceptance reports inside its catalogue delivery work. It already sells overlapping capabilities, so purchasing or subcontracting must not be assumed.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 supports bounded flat-field ToolSpec mappings and generic CSV output, but does not provide product enrichment, Merchant Center compliance, a universal mapping UI, CSV ingestion, or Shopify/PIM/ERP connectors.
leads.qualification_question: Would a repeatable JSON cleanup and acceptance report replace a measurable manual QA step in one current catalogue project?

leads.name: Vertica A/S
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its n8n directory profile describes an e-commerce agency. Its PIM service explicitly includes mapping source-system data, making data consistent, modelling product information and aligning data across channels.
leads.fit_inference: A possible PIM/product-data discovery interview or referral partner. The official profile lists larger project budgets, so a longer procurement cycle is plausible and it is not a first choice for a 14-day sale.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 does not implement PIM connectors, multi-source product modelling, cross-channel publication, or arbitrary catalogue mappings.
leads.qualification_question: Do smaller supplier feeds within your PIM projects still require repeated manual normalization or acceptance checks before import?

leads.name: Datamagnet
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its Apify profile lists e-commerce and product data, price monitoring, structured extraction, and integrations with Apify, Make, Zapier and custom APIs.
leads.fit_inference: A possible post-scrape workflow buyer or delivery partner if inconsistent JSON fields or repeated URLs cause measurable rework. This is inferred from its services, not a demonstrated purchasing need.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 does not normalize arbitrary scraper outputs or supply a native Make/Zapier integration. It accepts only the fixed supported JSON shape.
leads.qualification_question: In one current product-data workflow, how often do inconsistent scraper fields or duplicate URLs require manual repair before the next step?

leads.name: Parsedom Inc
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its Apify profile lists e-commerce and product data and end-to-end web scraping, processing, automation and visualization for structured and unstructured datasets.
leads.fit_inference: A possible peer interview, QA-tool buyer or referral partner for repeatable delivery checks. It already builds data solutions; its own development activity is not evidence of demand for this project.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 does not ingest arbitrary structured or unstructured source outputs, perform extraction, or generate dashboards; any paid scope must be limited to a confirmed JSON cleanup task.
leads.qualification_question: Which recurring delivery check takes the most manual time after scraping, and could you share a redacted input and expected output?

leads.name: Lexis Solutions
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its Apify profile lists e-commerce and products, multi-source integration, clean structured data and custom data workflows. It explicitly states that it does not subcontract projects.
leads.fit_inference: Discovery interview, referral or reusable-tool feedback candidate only. Do not pitch white-label subcontracting as an assumed fit because its public delivery policy rejects subcontracting.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 is not a general data-solution delivery platform and has no arbitrary source or field mappings. Whether an internal validation tool adds value is unknown.
leads.qualification_question: Would a reusable acceptance-check tool improve your own team's delivery without outsourcing any client work, or is the existing internal tooling sufficient?

leads.name: Hyperstack Studio
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its n8n profile offers data-stack setup, centralized data and workflow automation using n8n, Make, Airtable, Xano and BigQuery.
leads.fit_inference: A possible automation delivery buyer or referral partner, conditional on confirming a product-data workflow. The verified directory profile does not establish a catalogue-cleanup need.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 has no native connectors for its listed data stack and cannot normalize arbitrary retail or catalogue data.
leads.qualification_question: Do any current client workflows move product JSON between a scraper or supplier feed and an operational database, with a repeated cleanup or QA step?

leads.fit_inference: A possible retail automation interview or referral partner. General retail experience does not establish product feed or catalogue-cleanup demand.
leads.product_gap: v0.1.0 has no ERP/CRM connectors, broad document processing, or arbitrary retail schema support.
leads.qualification_question: Among your retail projects, is there a recurring product-data ingestion or acceptance task that is still repaired by hand?

leads.name: AOE Group
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its n8n profile lists custom nodes, complex API and data integrations, automated tests and a claimed reference connecting inventory, sales and fulfillment.
leads.fit_inference: A possible commerce automation discovery or referral partner. Larger listed project budgets suggest a potentially longer procurement cycle; the inventory reference does not prove a catalogue-cleanup need.

leads.qualification_question: Do small supplier datasets or edge integrations within larger projects create repeated product-data cleanup and acceptance work?

leads.observed_need_or_service: Its n8n profile lists ERP/CRM/API/database integration, central data hubs and validation of invoices and delivery notes, mainly for manufacturing clients.
leads.fit_inference: An adjacent integration referral candidate only until product master-data or catalogue synchronization is confirmed. Invoice validation is not evidence of product-data demand, and its larger project scope may lengthen procurement.

leads.name: Dots & Arrows
leads.observed_need_or_service: Its n8n profile offers end-to-end workflow delivery and tailored integrations for clients' tools, processes and data.
leads.fit_inference: A reserve discovery or referral candidate. No specific product feed, scraping or catalogue-cleanup use case has been verified; its larger listed project budgets may also make a small pilot a weak fit.
leads.product_gap: The published example uses a fixed catalog schema; the workbench supports validated flat-field ToolSpec mappings. It is not a general integration or automation platform.
leads.qualification_question: Is there a current product-data workflow involving Apify or supplier JSON with repeated cleanup work; if not, is a referral to such a team appropriate?

leads.name: Demand signal D01
leads.observed_need_or_service: Reports inconsistent supplier SKUs, column names, missing prices and stock formats; expresses interest in reliable mapping and validation at a non-enterprise price.
leads.fit_inference: A fixed supplier-to-target normalization and exception-review service could address part of the reported preparation work. Interest is not evidence of willingness to pay.
leads.product_gap: CSV ingestion, Shopify-ready export contracts, supplier SKU-to-Shopify Handle lookup and destination-specific validation are not established by the current fixed JSON normalization capability.
leads.qualification_question: For the most recent supplier update, what file, row count, cleanup time and remaining error would justify purchasing a fixed-scope preparation service?

leads.name: Demand signal D02
leads.observed_need_or_service: Reports that the last supplier update took roughly an hour, mostly matching supplier SKUs to Shopify Handles; distinguishes price and inventory import files.
leads.fit_inference: The measurable lookup/preparation time is a useful problem hypothesis for a repeatable mapping service, subject to sample-level validation.
leads.product_gap: Cross-file lookup, destination-specific partial-update semantics and generation of Shopify price/inventory imports exceed basic JSON normalization.
leads.qualification_question: Does the same lookup recur for the next supplier file, and would a reusable reviewed mapping remove enough time to justify a paid pilot?

leads.name: Demand signal D03
leads.observed_need_or_service: Describes reconciliation taking about an hour for a 3,000-SKU catalog, with SKU/Handle mismatch, damaged identifiers and unnecessary full-file updates as failure cases.
leads.fit_inference: Useful operator/expert evidence for identifier preservation and exception reporting; this does not establish that the handle is a merchant buyer.
leads.product_gap: SKU-to-Handle joins, previous/current file comparison and Shopify import correctness require capabilities beyond fixed JSON field normalization.
leads.qualification_question: Which reconciliation step remains manual today, and can its input and expected output be expressed as a fixed rule on a small masked sample?

leads.name: Demand signal D04
leads.observed_need_or_service: Reports product data entry as a major bottleneck when retailers add new SKUs; asks for an integration importing supplier descriptions, prices and inventory after wholesale purchase.
leads.fit_inference: Supplier catalog preparation may be one paid subproblem, but the stated desired outcome is a broader purchase-to-POS integration.
leads.product_gap: Supplier integrations, purchase triggers, product creation and live POS/store import are not covered by fixed JSON normalization.
leads.qualification_question: Would an import-ready reviewed file solve a paid portion of the bottleneck, or is an end-to-end supplier purchase integration essential?

leads.name: Demand signal D05
leads.observed_need_or_service: Is integrating UnoPim product attributes with Shopify metafields and asks about text, numeric, select/multiselect, boolean and multiple-value mapping, including later type changes.
leads.fit_inference: Field/type normalization is relevant to a preflight step; this may represent an integrator ICP rather than an end merchant. Role and buying authority are unverified.
leads.product_gap: Shopify definition lifecycle, schema migration, dynamic mapping and synchronization execution are outside the established JSON normalizer scope.
leads.qualification_question: Is there a fixed typed mapping and representative JSON batch that could be validated before the existing sync, without modifying Shopify definitions?

leads.name: Demand signal D06
leads.observed_need_or_service: Reports 10,516 variants and 200-plus suppliers, manual Supplier SKU/cost/tax work, and an existing Inventory Planner workflow used to create files for Shopify purchase-order imports.
leads.fit_inference: A real, already tooled operating environment with file preparation work, but the broad pain includes purchasing and receiving rather than normalization alone. Existing tool use does not prove budget for this offer.
leads.product_gap: PO lifecycle, procurement, receiving, multi-warehouse operations, cross-system reconciliation and cost handling substantially exceed current capability.
leads.qualification_question: After the purchase-order import changes, what manual file preparation still remains and can one supplier's repeatable batch be isolated?

leads.name: Demand signal D07
leads.observed_need_or_service: Wants supplier-specific SKUs stored separately from store SKUs and automatically carried into purchase orders to avoid manual entry.
leads.fit_inference: A supplier-to-store mapping table may be relevant, but the desired result is native purchase-order linkage. Continued need and willingness to accept file preparation are unknown.
leads.product_gap: Persistent SKU relationships, Shopify metafields and PO linkage are not established fixed JSON normalization capabilities.
leads.qualification_question: Is maintaining the supplier-to-store identifier map still manual, and would a reviewed mapping file help without native PO automation?

leads.name: Demand signal D08
leads.observed_need_or_service: Needs thousands of supplier JSON products safely synced to Shopify: SKU matching, changed-field updates, duplicate-match handling and action logs; already has a basic Make workflow.
leads.fit_inference: The explicit JSON input is unusually close to the current artifact's input shape, but this is an old archived request and the full desired solution is much broader.
leads.product_gap: Cross-dataset identity resolution, diffing, Shopify creation/update, bulk orchestration and persistent action logs are not established by the current normalizer.
leads.qualification_question: If this need still exists, can a pre-sync JSON cleanup/exception step provide standalone value inside the existing workflow?

leads.name: Demand signal D09
leads.observed_need_or_service: Wants daily POS CSV stock updates applied only to matching Shopify SKUs, while ignoring source products that are not in the store.
leads.fit_inference: Field and number normalization could be a small preparation step. The core request is a join plus conditional inventory update, and current demand is unverified.
leads.product_gap: CSV adapter, external SKU lookup and conditional Shopify inventory writes exceed fixed JSON normalization.
leads.qualification_question: Does the current workflow already handle matching, and is there still any recurring input-format or validation problem before that step?

leads.name: Demand signal D10
leads.observed_need_or_service: Wants supplier Excel columns placed into a fixed product/price template, selling-price calculations and a workflow that can handle a different source layout each time.
leads.fit_inference: Repeatable fixed mappings are a good fit hypothesis; adaptive schema detection is a separate unproven capability. This is old evidence, not a current buying request.
leads.product_gap: Excel ingestion/export, dynamic source detection, margin-calculation scope and email delivery are not established current capabilities.
leads.qualification_question: Can the recurring inputs be reduced to a finite set of approved schemas, and which fixed transformation currently consumes time?

leads.name: Demand signal D11
leads.observed_need_or_service: Manages roughly 10,000 products across eight brands with high monthly turnover; needs missing content collected, products formatted/imported and discontinued lines handled.
leads.fit_inference: Catalog normalization is only a subproblem. The main request includes missing data acquisition and ongoing catalog management, making this weak for the initial narrow offer.
leads.product_gap: PDF extraction, scraping/enrichment, images, discontinued-product detection and recurring Shopify synchronization exceed current capability.
leads.qualification_question: Is there already a structured supplier feed whose preparation alone is costly, separate from collecting missing descriptions and images?

experiment_price_hypothesis.limitations: Arithmetic scenario for one paid-plan external run, not a forecast. Actual costs, applicable tier prices, refunds, settlement, and customer demand are unverified.

facts.statement: PPE platform profit is documented as 0.8 times eligible event revenue minus platform costs. Paid-plan revenue and costs count; free-plan users do not contribute creator revenue.
facts.experiment_implication: Track independent eligible paid-plan demand separately from free adoption, owner tests, grants, and promotional activity. Platform eligibility is not final cash settlement.

facts.statement: Monetization setup requires billing and payment details. Payout additionally requires completed identity verification/KYC.
facts.experiment_implication: Verify actual readiness before starting Day 1. AI must not invent legal identity, submit fabricated documents, or claim that readiness has been checked.

facts.statement: Published payout guidance uses the previous month's profits: invoices on day 11, automatic approval on day 14 if untouched, and payouts on days 21-25. Only legitimate users who have already paid are included in payout invoices.
facts.experiment_implication: A proposed 2026-10-21 through 2026-11-03 experiment crosses two earning months. October usage maps to the November payout cycle; November usage maps to the December cycle. Neither a charge event nor estimated profit proves cash received.

facts.statement: The payout guide lists USD 20 for PayPal and Wise and USD 100 for other methods. The September 15 Store terms list USD 20 for PayPal and USD 100 for other options, without separately naming Wise.
facts.experiment_implication: Record the discrepancy and verify the selected method in Console or with Apify. Do not promise a USD 20 Wise payout or any payout within 14 days.

facts.statement: The platform supports automatic start and default-dataset-item events. Charge for saved, accessible results and respect run spending limits.
facts.experiment_implication: Audit synthetic and custom event paths for duplicate billing before enabling the hypothesis. Retain run IDs, delivered counts, charged counts, actual event fees, and errors as evidence.

facts.statement: Significant pricing changes normally have a 14-day notice and monthly restriction. The setup guide says the waiting period does not apply when there are no paying users.
facts.experiment_implication: Hold the initial price fixed for the cohort and test positioning or use cases instead of assuming daily live price increases are available.

facts.statement: Store terms restrict off-platform product/service promotion in Actor and Store content and the use of payment gateways outside Apify.
facts.experiment_implication: Keep paid Actor use and checkout within Apify. Do not insert an external paid-service or deposit link in the Actor README, description, issues, or reviews.

facts.statement: The official monetization overview describes separate eligibility for per-request agentic payments, including PPE without added usage billing, limited permissions, no Standby mode, and completed KYC.
facts.experiment_implication: Treat agentic-payment availability as a conditional distribution capability, not as a reason to self-fund purchases or claim independent demand.

evidence_ladder.name: successful_external_delivery
evidence_ladder.required: A real external user receives useful results. Free usage may qualify for delivery, but not paid demand.

evidence_ladder.name: eligible_external_paid_usage_provisional
evidence_ladder.required: Independent customer, positive actual eligible event charges, successful accessible delivery, and exclusion of owner/test/subsidized activity. Store evidence by run and anonymized customer identifier.

evidence_ladder.name: settled_platform_earnings
evidence_ladder.required: Platform settlement or payout-invoice evidence, with refund and unpaid-invoice adjustments recorded.

evidence_ladder.name: cash_received
evidence_ladder.required: Actual receipt in the owner's payout account, recorded separately from charges and estimated profit.

explicit_non_revenue_metrics: estimated demand from competitor public statistics
pricingFacts.execution_boundary: This artifact is a dated plan input. No messages were sent, accounts created, billing altered, paid services called, or scheduled execution configured. Unknown channel automation permission means read-only research until verified.
